rationale:
Split into three children. The supplied mollification proof contains three independent obligations, each reusable on its own:
- Step 2 (normalized mollifier) → child normalized_mollifier. Mathlib's ContDiffBump.normed and integral_normed are outside the frozen import closure (checked: Unknown constant), so a hand-normalized bump has to be proved anyway.
- Step 3(a)–(d) (C^∞ approximant by convolution) → child mollify_deriv_approx. It gives the support bound in cthickening δ (tsupport φ) and the uniform directional-derivative bound. It uses one radius r = min r₀ δ instead of the sequence δ/(ℓ+1); the argument is the same, re-indexed.
- The ε-estimate of step 5 → child pairing_uniform_limit. If the pairing with G ∈ L¹(K) vanishes on uniform approximants, it vanishes in the limit.

A childless node must be one appended theorem with no helper declarations. Factoring isolates the convolution API work from the measure-theoretic limit. Each child and the parent glue becomes a short proof of 10–40 Lean lines, instead of one monolithic proof of about 130 lines.

Parent glue (steps 1, 4, 6 and the reductions in step 5):
1. Pick δ > 0 with K_δ := cthickening δ (tsupport φ) ⊆ D (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). K_δ is compact and closed, hence measurable, and G is integrable on it (LocallyIntegrableOn.integrableOn_compact_subset).
2. Let e := basisFun i = single i 1 (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply) and f := ∂ₑφ. f is continuous and vanishes off tsupport φ (fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport). It has compact support, so it is bounded (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous).
3. ∫ G f = ∫_{K_δ} G f (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
4. Apply pairing_uniform_limit on K_δ. For each ε > 0, mollify_deriv_approx(φ, δ, e, ε) gives ψ; take g := ∂ₑψ, which is continuous with |f − g| ≤ ε. Then ∫_{K_δ} G g = ∫_D G g, because g = 0 on D \ K_δ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero). This is 0 by the smooth-test hypothesis with a := ψ (tsupport ψ ⊆ K_δ ⊆ D) and j := i.

subproblems.title: Normalized smooth mollifier on ℝⁿ with support in a given ball
subproblems.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ and every r > 0 there is ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure) such that ρ is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), ρ has compact support, ρ(x) ≥ 0 for all x, ∫_{ℝⁿ} ρ = 1, and support ρ ⊆ B_r(0) (the open ball of radius r about 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → ∃ ρ : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ρ ∧ HasCompactSupport ρ ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ρ x) ∧ ∫ x, ρ x = 1 ∧ support ρ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) r
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof ("Mollifiers": a ContDiffBump B_r centred at 0 with rIn = r/2, rOut = r, normalized by hand as ϱ_r := (∫B_r)⁻¹·B_r). Mathlib's ContDiffBump.normed / ContDiffBump.integral_normed live in Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/BumpFunction/Normed.lean, which is NOT in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission, so the normalization is done by hand.
Notation: ℝⁿ = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure volume; ∫ means ∫ ... ∂volume.
1. Fix n ∈ ℕ and r > 0. Euclid n is a finite-dimensional real normed space, so the instance HasContDiffBump (Euclid n) is found by instance search (ExistsContDiffBumpBase.instHasContDiffBumpOfFiniteDimensionalReal; HasContDiffBump is a Prop, so which instance is found does not matter). Let B : ContDiffBump (0 : Euclid n) be the bump with rIn := r/2 and rOut := r; the side conditions 0 < r/2 and r/2 < r are half_pos hr and half_lt_self hr. Write B(x) for its value (the coercion Euclid n → ℝ).
2. Properties of B. (i) ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) B (ContDiffBump.contDiff holds for every order in ℕ∞). (ii) B is continuous (ContDiffBump.continuous). (iii) 0 ≤ B(x) for every x (ContDiffBump.nonneg). (iv) support B = ball 0 r (ContDiffBump.support_eq, since rOut = r). (v) HasCompactSupport B (ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport; Euclid n is finite-dimensional).
3. B is integrable: it is continuous with compact support and volume is finite on compact sets (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport with 2(ii), 2(v)).
4. I := ∫ B(x) dx is positive. By integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg (B ≥ 0 by 2(iii), integrable by 3), 0 < I if and only if 0 < volume (support B). By 2(iv), support B = ball 0 r, and volume (ball 0 r) > 0 because r > 0 and Lebesgue measure gives positive mass to nonempty open sets (Metric.measure_ball_pos volume 0 hr). Hence I > 0; in particular I ≠ 0 and I⁻¹ ≥ 0.
5. Define ρ(x) := I⁻¹ · B(x), i.e. ρ = fun x => (∫ y, B y)⁻¹ * B x. Then:
 (a) ρ is C^∞ (order (⊤ : ℕ∞)): it is the product of the constant function I⁻¹ and B (contDiff_const.mul with 2(i)).
 (b) ρ has compact support: support ρ ⊆ support B, and HasCompactSupport.mul_left applied to 2(v) gives HasCompactSupport ρ.
 (c) ρ(x) ≥ 0 for every x: mul_nonneg of I⁻¹ ≥ 0 (inv_nonneg, step 4) and B(x) ≥ 0 (2(iii)).
 (d) ∫ ρ = I⁻¹ · ∫ B = I⁻¹ · I = 1, by integral_const_mul and inv_mul_cancel₀ (I ≠ 0, step 4).
 (e) support ρ ⊆ support B = ball 0 r, by Function.support_mul_subset_right (the support of x ↦ c · B(x) is contained in the support of B) and 2(iv).
6. Thus ρ is smooth, compactly supported, nonnegative, has integral 1 and support ρ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) r, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take the ContDiffBump B centred at 0 with rIn = r/2, rOut = r: smooth, nonnegative, support B = ball 0 r, compact support, integrable.
I := ∫B > 0 by integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg, since volume (ball 0 r) > 0.
ρ := I⁻¹·B is smooth, compactly supported, nonnegative, has ∫ρ = I⁻¹·I = 1, and support ρ ⊆ support B = ball 0 r.

subproblems.title: Mollification approximates a C¹_c function in directional-derivative sup norm with support control
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C¹ with compact support, δ > 0, v ∈ ℝⁿ and ε > 0. Then there is ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) with compact support such that tsupport ψ ⊆ cthickening δ (tsupport φ) (the closed δ-neighbourhood of the topological support of φ) and |Dψ(x)v − Dφ(x)v| ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝⁿ (Df(x)v = fderiv ℝ f x v).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (φ : Euclid n → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → HasCompactSupport φ → ∀ (δ : ℝ), 0 < δ → ∀ (v : Euclid n) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ ψ : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ψ ∧ HasCompactSupport ψ ∧ tsupport ψ ⊆ cthickening δ (tsupport φ) ∧ ∀ x, |fderiv ℝ ψ x v - fderiv ℝ φ x v| ≤ ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof ((a) smoothness, (b) support, (c) derivative of the convolution, (d) uniform convergence), for one mollification radius. The parent uses r_ℓ = δ/(ℓ+1) and takes ℓ with r_ℓ ≤ r₀. Here we take directly r := min r₀ δ for the given ε, which is exactly what step 3(d) needs. The mollifier of step 2 is the sibling lemma dgcr_stc_exists_normalized_mollifier.
Notation: ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure volume; ∂ᵥf(x) := Df(x)v = fderiv ℝ f x v; convolution (ρ ⋆ f)(x) := ∫ ρ(t)·f(x − t) dt, i.e. Mathlib's convolution ρ f (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume.
1. Uniform continuity of ∂ᵥφ. φ is C¹, so Dφ = fderiv ℝ φ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv with 1 ≠ 0). Dφ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv). Let g(x) := ∂ᵥφ(x) = fderiv ℝ φ x v. Then g is continuous (Continuous.clm_apply with the constant function v). It has compact support by HasCompactSupport.comp_left, since evaluation at v, L ↦ L v, sends 0 to 0. A continuous function with compact support is uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). By Metric.uniformContinuous_iff there is r₀ > 0 with dist (g a) (g b) < ε whenever dist a b < r₀.
2. Mollifier. Put r := min r₀ δ; then r > 0 (lt_min, since r₀ > 0 and δ > 0), r ≤ r₀ and r ≤ δ. The sibling lemma dgcr_stc_exists_normalized_mollifier, applied to n and r, gives ρ : Euclid n → ℝ with: ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ρ, HasCompactSupport ρ, ρ ≥ 0 pointwise, ∫ ρ = 1, and support ρ ⊆ ball 0 r. ρ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous), hence locally integrable (Continuous.locallyIntegrable).
3. Define ψ := ρ ⋆ φ = convolution ρ φ (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume.
4. Smoothness. ψ is C^∞ (order (⊤ : ℕ∞)) by HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left with L = lsmul ℝ ℝ. Its hypotheses: the left factor ρ is compactly supported and ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞); the right factor φ is locally integrable, being continuous (C¹; Continuous.locallyIntegrable).
5. Support. By support_convolution_subset, support ψ ⊆ support ρ + support φ. Let z ∈ support ψ and write z = a + b with a ∈ support ρ and b ∈ support φ (Set.mem_add). Then ‖a‖ < r since support ρ ⊆ ball 0 r, and b ∈ tsupport φ (subset_tsupport). Hence dist z b = ‖(a + b) − b‖ = ‖a‖ < r ≤ δ. So z ∈ cthickening δ (tsupport φ) (mem_cthickening_of_dist_le). Thus support ψ ⊆ cthickening δ (tsupport φ). The closed thickening is closed (isClosed_cthickening), so tsupport ψ = closure (support ψ) ⊆ cthickening δ (tsupport φ) (closure_minimal).
6. Compact support. tsupport φ is compact (HasCompactSupport φ), so cthickening δ (tsupport φ) is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; Euclid n is a proper space). tsupport ψ is closed (isClosed_tsupport) and contained in it by step 5. Hence tsupport ψ is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), i.e. HasCompactSupport ψ.
7. Derivative of ψ. Fix x. HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right applies with L = lsmul ℝ ℝ: ρ is locally integrable, and φ is compactly supported and ContDiff ℝ 1. It says ψ has Fréchet derivative convolution ρ (fderiv ℝ φ) (ContinuousLinearMap.precompR (Euclid n) (lsmul ℝ ℝ)) volume x at x. Hence fderiv ℝ ψ x equals this (HasFDerivAt.fderiv). Evaluate at v with convolution_precompR_apply, using that ρ is locally integrable and Dφ is compactly supported and continuous (step 1). This gives fderiv ℝ ψ x v = convolution ρ g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x = (ρ ⋆ g)(x).
8. Estimate. Keep x fixed. For every y ∈ ball x r, dist y x < r ≤ r₀, so dist (g y) (g x) < ε by step 1. Apply dist_convolution_le with these inputs: 0 ≤ ε; R := r with support ρ ⊆ ball 0 r; ρ ≥ 0 pointwise and ∫ ρ = 1; g AE-strongly measurable (it is continuous: Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable); z₀ := g(x); and dist (g y) z₀ ≤ ε for all y ∈ ball x r. It yields dist ((ρ ⋆ g)(x)) (g(x)) ≤ ε. By step 7 and Real.dist_eq, this is |fderiv ℝ ψ x v − fderiv ℝ φ x v| ≤ ε.
9. ψ has the four required properties: smooth (step 4), compactly supported (step 6), tsupport ψ ⊆ cthickening δ (tsupport φ) (step 5), and the derivative bound for every x (step 8). ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂ᵥφ is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous: pick r₀ > 0 with |∂ᵥφ(a) − ∂ᵥφ(b)| < ε when dist a b < r₀.
r := min r₀ δ; the sibling lemma gives a normalized mollifier ρ (smooth, compact support, ρ ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1, support ⊆ ball 0 r); ψ := ρ ⋆ φ.
ψ is smooth (contDiff_convolution_left); support ψ ⊆ ball 0 r + tsupport φ ⊆ cthickening δ (tsupport φ), a closed compact set, so tsupport ψ ⊆ cthickening δ (tsupport φ) and ψ has compact support.
dist_convolution_le with the uniform-continuity modulus gives |∂ᵥψ(x) − ∂ᵥφ(x)| ≤ ε for every x.

subproblems.title: An L¹ pairing that vanishes on uniform approximants vanishes in the limit
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, K ⊆ ℝⁿ measurable, G : ℝⁿ → ℝ integrable on K, f : ℝⁿ → ℝ AE-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to K with |f(x)| ≤ C for all x ∈ K. Suppose that for every ε > 0 there is g : ℝⁿ → ℝ, AE-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to K, with |f(x) − g(x)| ≤ ε for all x ∈ K and ∫_K G·g = 0. Then ∫_K G·f = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid n)) (G f : Euclid n → ℝ) (C : ℝ), MeasurableSet K → IntegrableOn G K volume → AEStronglyMeasurable f (volume.restrict K) → (∀ x ∈ K, |f x| ≤ C) → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Euclid n → ℝ, AEStronglyMeasurable g (volume.restrict K) ∧ (∀ x ∈ K, |f x - g x| ≤ ε) ∧ ∫ x in K, G x * g x = 0) → ∫ x in K, G x * f x = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof. There, the integrals over D are reduced to integrals over the compact K_δ, and |∫ G·∂ᵢφ| = |∫_{K_δ} G·(∂ᵢφ − ∂ᵢφ_ℓ)| ≤ ε·∫_{K_δ}|G| for every ε > 0, so the integral vanishes. Here this is stated abstractly for a measurable set K, a bounded AE-strongly measurable f, and approximants g that G annihilates.
Notation: ∫_K h means ∫ x in K, h x (volume restricted to K).
1. Put M := ∫_K |G|. Then M ≥ 0 (integral_nonneg). Every pointwise bound "for all x ∈ K" used below holds almost everywhere for volume restricted to K (ae_restrict_of_forall_mem, since K is measurable).
2. Claim: |∫_K G·f| ≤ ε·M for every ε > 0. Fix ε > 0 and take g from the hypothesis: g AE-strongly measurable for volume restricted to K, |f(x) − g(x)| ≤ ε for x ∈ K, and ∫_K G·g = 0.
 (a) G·f is integrable on K by Integrable.mul_bdd: G is integrable on K, f is AE-strongly measurable, and ‖f‖ ≤ C a.e. on K (step 1).
 (b) G·g is integrable on K. For x ∈ K, |g(x)| = |f(x) − (f(x) − g(x))| ≤ |f(x)| + |f(x) − g(x)| ≤ C + ε (abs_sub). So Integrable.mul_bdd applies with the bound C + ε.
 (c) ∫_K G·f = ∫_K G·f − ∫_K G·g = ∫_K (G·f − G·g) = ∫_K G·(f − g). This uses ∫_K G·g = 0, integral_sub with (a) and (b), and mul_sub.
 (d) For x ∈ K, |G(x)·(f(x) − g(x))| = |G(x)|·|f(x) − g(x)| ≤ |G(x)|·ε. The function x ↦ |G(x)|·ε is integrable on K (Integrable.norm, Integrable.mul_const). So norm_integral_le_of_norm_le gives |∫_K G·(f − g)| ≤ ∫_K |G|·ε = M·ε (integral_mul_const). With (c), |∫_K G·f| ≤ ε·M.
3. Conclusion. Suppose a := |∫_K G·f| > 0. Apply step 2 with ε := a / (2(M + 1)) > 0, which gives a ≤ a·M / (2(M + 1)). But 0 ≤ M < 2(M + 1) and a > 0, so a·M / (2(M + 1)) < a, a contradiction. Hence ∫_K G·f = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: G·f and G·g are integrable on K (Integrable.mul_bdd; |g| ≤ C + ε on K).
∫_K G f = ∫_K G (f − g), so |∫_K G f| ≤ ε·∫_K |G| (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le).
Since ε > 0 is arbitrary and ∫_K |G| < ∞, ∫_K G f = 0 (choose ε = |∫_K G f| / (2(M+1)) for a contradiction).
